speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Members may also access this material through the SG PARL MP mobile app.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Annex lists the amendments to be made via this Bill, which I will take Members through.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clause 2 of the Bill makes two amendments to section 2 of the Interpretation Act 1965.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Second, a new general provision will be inserted, which provides that definitions in written laws apply unless the context otherwise requires.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This obviates the need to repeat similar provisions in each definition provision in legislation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It will also specify that the fees that CAAS is currently empowered to prescribe under section 9(1)(t) can be either one-time or periodic in nature.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I now come to the amendments to the Children and Young Persons Act 1993 (CYPA).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The CYPA was amended by the Children and Young Persons (Amendment) Act 2019.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Sections 27 and 55 of the 2019 Amendment Act have not been brought into force.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clause 4 of the Bill makes substantively the same amendments as those sections, but updates references to other statutory provisions that have since been renumbered in the 2020 Revised Edition of Acts.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It will also allow the First Schedule and the Second Schedule of the CYPA to be brought into force separately.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Turning to the next amendment, clause 5 deletes the definition of "company" and "corporation" in section 63(1) of the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore Act 2009 (CAAS Act), because they are unnecessary in the context of the CAAS Act.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Next, clause 6 of the Bill amends four provisions in the Copyright Act 2021 (CA).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The first amendment is to section 193 of the CA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The CA makes a distinction between "works" and "performances", and recognises that both "works" and "performances", can be fairly used for the purposes of criticism or review.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Where works are concerned, section 193 of the CA provides that any underlying materials that are incorporated in works are deemed fairly used if the works themselves are fairly used for the purposes of criticism or review.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: However, this deeming provision does not currently extend to performances.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Second, section 285 of the CA provides that a "public act", which is an act done for the service of the Government, by the Government or by an authorised person, is an exception to copyright infringement.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Section 285(2)(a) currently provides that the Government is to inform the relevant rights owner as soon as practicable after the public act is done.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Section 285(2)(a) will be amended to signpost that the means by which the Government is to inform a rights owner of the public act is set out in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Third, section 301 provides how copies of a work or a recording of a protected performance should be notated.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Subsection (1)(a) will be amended to make clear that the "copy" referred to in that subsection refers only to a copy of a "sound recording" and not other types of works.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Fourth, the CA, which came into force on 21 November 2021, introduced the right for authors to be identified in relation to the public use of certain works.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Section 377(2)(b) provides a transitional arrangement for existing works made before 21 November 2021, whereby the first copyright owner's initial assignee or licensee is exempted from having to identify the author of the existing work.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Section 377(2)(b) will be extended to exempt: (a)	the first copyright owner and (b)	subsequent assignees and licensees beyond the first copyright owner's initial assignee or licensee as well.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This amendment will put the first copyright owner, initial assignee and licensee, and subsequent assignees and licensees of an existing work on equal footing.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Next, I will address the amendments to the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act 2020 (COTMA).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As this House is aware, Part 2 and Part 8 of COTMA introduced reliefs for individuals and businesses affected by COVID-19 in certain contracts and situations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Panel of Assessors for COVID-19 (Temporary Relief) (PACT) and its supporting Registry were formed in April 2020 and heard disputes relating to Part 2 and Part 8.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This helped parties avoid costly and time-consuming litigation, relating to contractual disagreements arising from COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: With the COVID-19 situation having stabilised, these urgent reliefs, introduced during very exceptional times, have run their course and are no longer necessary.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Part 2 and Part 8 reliefs are no longer available – they are only applied for prescribed periods, the last of which came to an end on 28 February 2022.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is now time to wind down the PACT Registry.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clause 7 therefore provides that applications which remain pending at a prescribed date will be deemed to be withdrawn.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Determinations and subsequent determinations also cannot be made after a prescribed date.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In this regard, there are 20 applications concerning construction and supply contracts which remain outstanding, which will be deemed withdrawn when this amendment comes into effect.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The withdrawal does not affect the substantive rights of the parties.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For construction and supply contracts, the service of a valid NFR would entitle the affected party to two categories of relief: (i) a moratorium against legal and enforcement action, and (ii) a statutory defence against damages for delays or breaches which are materially caused by COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As regards applications relating to the statutory defence, the Assessors' role has always been limited to assessing whether the NFR was valid.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The party receiving the NFR could choose to challenge the statutory defence if it is invoked by the serving party in the course of proceedings before a court, tribunal or adjudicator.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This right to challenge the availability of the defence before a court, tribunal or adjudicator continues to be available even after these applications for Assessors' applications are deemed withdrawn.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clause 7 therefore validates applications made from 20 April 2022 to 30 April 2022.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Section 97(5) of the Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Act 2021 (GEWCA) introduced a new section 7(2) to the Customs Act.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This section, which has not been commenced, stated that customs officers are to be provided with "such staves, guns, ammunition and other accoutrements which may be prescribed".

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clause 8 of the present Bill inserts a new section 6A to the Customs Act in place of section 7(2).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Section 6A is substantively similar to section 7(2), save that the word "staves" is replaced with "batons" and the arms to be provided need not be prescribed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Consequently, the amendments made by section 97(5) of GEWCA is superseded and deleted.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I now come to clause 9, which amends the Extradition Act 1968 (EA).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Extradition Act was amended in April this year to introduce, amongst others, a new mechanism for fugitives to consent to their extradition.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clause 9 makes several clarifications related to that new mechanism: (a) first, that the Magistrate's power to remand a fugitive who has consented to his or her surrender includes the power to remand such a fugitive who is provisionally arrested and where the formal extradition request from the Requesting State is pending; (b) second, a consenting fugitive does not need to additionally waive his or her right to apply for a review of the committal order; and (c) third, that the power to re-arrest fugitives who escaped during their arrest or from custody covers fugitives who have consented to their surrender.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This power of arrest is exercised in the same manner as that involving a person accused of an arrestable offence against the law in force in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Next, clause 10 makes amendments to section 29 of the Gas Act 2001, which provides for the inspection, maintenance, repair or renewal, of any part of a gas installation or any part of a gas service pipe linking a gas service isolation valve to the gas installation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The amendments will clarify that the Energy Market Authority will prescribe persons responsible for the inspection, maintenance, repair or renewal of such parts by way of an order in the Gazette; and section 4(b) of the Energy (Resilience Measures and Miscellaneous Amendments) Act 2021, which has not commenced, deletes the existing section 29(4) of the Gas Act and substitutes it with new sections 29(4), 29(5) and 29(6).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The new section 29(4) of the Gas Act relates to obligations on the gas transporter to inspect gas installations or gas service pipes and to notify certain persons to carry out maintenance, repair or renewal following the inspection.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This Bill will amend section 29(4)(c) to clarify that the "person" the gas transporter is to notify, is the person prescribed under section 29(3) of the Gas Act to be responsible for such maintenance, repair or renewal, if that person is not the gas transporter.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I now turn to Clause 11, which amends the Second Schedule of the Land Transport Authority of Singapore Act 1995 (LTA Act).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Second Schedule sets out taxes, fees and charges to be paid to the Land Transport Revenue Account.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Paragraph 1 currently relates to fees imposed under the Parking Places Act (PPA).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This includes fees under Part 3 of the PPA, which was repealed by the Share Mobility Enterprises (Control and Licensing) Act 2020.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Paragraph 1 of the Second Schedule of the LTA Act will be amended to reinstate the original wording that existed before Part 3 of the PPA was introduced.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: A new paragraph 26, relating to fees and charges prescribed under the Small Motorised Vehicles (Safety) Act 2020 (SMVA) will be inserted to the Second Schedule of the LTA Act.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The SMVA originally made this amendment, but it could not be commenced as there was an existing provision with the same number.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Next, I come to amendments relating to the Medicines Act 1975.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clause 12 deletes provisions in the Medicines Act relating to intellectual property obligations for pharmaceutical products.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Those obligations are now found in the Health Products Act 2007 and its regulations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The provisions in the Medicines Act are therefore unnecessary.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In addition, section 76(1) of the Medicines Act 1975 currently provides for the repeal of the Medicines (Advertisement and Sale) Act 1955 (MASA) and the Sale of Drugs Act 1914 (SDA) in the same subsection such that they must be repealed together.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I will now turn to the next amendment, which is to the Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act 2000 (MACMA).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Under section 41(1) of MACMA, when Singapore makes a request for mutual assistance or receives a request for assistance in criminal matters, the Attorney-General must notify the Minister.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Upon receipt of the notice, the Minister may instruct the Attorney-General to take or not to take action that the Minister thinks is in or against the interests of the sovereignty, security or public order of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As part of Singapore's commitment to work with our international partners to combat crime, it is important to ensure Singapore's compliance with international law standards for the timely prioritisation and execution of mutual legal assistance requests.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In this regard, the Minister authorises public officers of appropriate seniority and experience to review such notices from the Attorney-General, in accordance with common law principles.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Under these common law principles, which have been upheld by our Courts, a Minister may authorise the exercise of such functions by his or her officers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Nevertheless, as the Minister is responsible to Parliament, the Minister must ensure that such functions are carried out by duly experienced and qualified officers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This has been the case in the context of section 41 notices under MACMA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Minister will nonetheless continue to personally exercise his power for notices as the circumstances require.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Next, I will touch on the amendment to the Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation Funds Act 2014 (PMGFA).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Section 16(1)(a) of the PMGFA provides that a Pioneer or Merdeka Generation Senior is eligible for a cash grant to be credited to his or her MediSave or other CPF account during a prescribed period.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: However, there are situations where an individual is determined to be a Pioneer or Merdeka Generation Senior after the prescribed period, after verification by the Appeals Panel.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clause 14 also validates the cash grants that have already been credited in such situations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I now come to the Police Force Act 2004.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: First, under section 69 of the Police Force Act, the Commissioner or Deputy Commissioner of Police is responsible for the promotion of a special Police Officer of the rank of Deputy Superintendent to the rank of Superintendent.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: However, the Minister for Home Affairs is responsible for the appointment, reduction in rank, dismissal or discharge of a superintendent.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clause 15 of the Bill amends section 69 such that the Minister for Home Affairs is the approving authority for the promotion of a special Police Officer to the rank of Superintendent.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This ensures that the approving authority for the appointment of, promotion to, reduction of rank, discharge and dismissal of special Police Officers of the same rank is the same person.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Second, clause 15 validates certain previous promotions that have been made by the Minister for Home Affairs or the Permanent Secretary of MHA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To explain, in previous years, the promotions of special Police Officers from the rank of Inspector to Assistant Superintendent were approved pursuant to the Minister's powers under section 69(1) delegated to the Permanent Secretary to the Ministry of Home Affairs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These promotions should have been approved by the Commissioner or Deputy of Commissioner for Police instead.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I now come to the amendments to the Protection from Harassment Act 2014 (POHA).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clause 16 of the Bill makes four amendments to POHA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: First, the definition of "court" in section 2(1) currently states that "court" for the purposes of sections 12 and 13 and Division 2 of Part 3 means "a District Court (including the Protection from Harassment Court) or a Family Court".

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These provisions provide for Protection Orders, Expedited Protection Orders and orders relating to false statements to be granted.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Aside from the District Court and the Family Court, other Courts such as the General Division of the High Court can make orders under these provisions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The definition of "court" will hence be amended to "a court of competent jurisdiction".

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This will ensure that all Courts which may grant Protection Orders, Expedited Protection Orders and orders relating to false statements are included within the definition of "court".

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Second, under section 6 of POHA, public service workers are accorded enhanced protection against harassment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Some volunteers provide services similar to public service workers and also frequently interact with the public in the course of providing such services.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Sections 6(5) and 6(6) of POHA will be amended to allow such volunteers to be prescribed as "public service workers", which will accord such volunteers the same enhanced protection against harassment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Third, section 13(5) of POHA currently provides that there shall be no appeal against a decision relating to Expedited Protection Orders made by the District Court under section 13.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As decisions relating to an Expedited Protection Order may also be made by other Courts such as the Family Court or High Court, clause 16 amends section 13(5) to replace "District Court" with "court" to make it clear that all such decisions made under section 13 are not appealable, no matter which Court makes the decision.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Lastly, clause 16 makes clarificatory amendments to section 16I of POHA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Section 16I(4) provides that other civil proceedings may be commenced in the Protection from Harassment Court only if "related to" Part 3 proceedings under POHA in the PHC.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clause 16 of the Bill amends section 16I to define when civil proceedings are related to Part 3 proceedings.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This will enable PUB to benefit from the contributions of a more diverse Board.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I now come to the amendments of the Registered Designs Act 2000 (RDA).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Section 30A of the RDA, introduced by the Intellectual Property (Amendment) Act 2022, provides express legal effect to disclaimers filed with the Registrar.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Disclaimers are indications or statements that limit the rights conferred by registration under section 30 of the RDA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This means that section 30A only confers express legal effect to disclaimers filed on or after 26 May 2022, the commencement date of section 30A of the RDA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Next, clause 19 of the Bill makes two amendments to the Sentosa Development Corporation Act 1972 (SDCA).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: First, it will be explicitly clarified that the definition of "Sentosa" in section 2 includes islands that become contiguous with the island of Sentosa because of land reclamation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This, in turn, clarifies that Sentosa Cove falls within the definition of "Sentosa" as part of the land now known as Sentosa Cove used to be a separate island from Sentosa until the narrow channel that ran between the two islands was reclaimed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Second, section 6(2) of the SDCA will be amended to provide that any person acting under the direction of the Sentosa Development Corporation (SDC) will be repaid out of the SDC's funds for any expense incurred.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is for consistency with section 6(1) of the SDCA where any member, employee or any other person acting under the direction of SDC is protected from personal liability while acting under the direction.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: A Notice to Attend Court is one of the modes of initiating criminal proceedings.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is a notice requiring a person to attend Court at a specified time and date.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Currently, where an accused person fails to attend Court on the date stated in a Notice to Attend Court, there are 15 Acts that require an accused person to show cause as to why he or she should not be punished with a fine or imprisonment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: However, other statutes, notably the Criminal Procedure Code 2010, do not have a similar show cause procedure.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This means that no additional penalty is imposed on the accused person for the failure to attend Court pursuant to a Notice to Attend Court, even without cause.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Court will continue to be able to issue a warrant of arrest to secure the accused person's attendance in Court.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Further, failure to attend Court will ordinarily be taken into account by the Court as an aggravating factor which may justify an increase in the sentence for the underlying offence.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Next, the Insolvency, Restructuring and Dissolution Act 2018 (IRDA).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: When it was introduced, it consolidated corporate and personal insolvency laws found in the Bankruptcy Act and Companies Act in one place.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The IRDA made consequential amendments to several Acts to replace references to the Bankruptcy Act and Companies Act with references to the IRDA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have since identified some inadvertent omissions in these references, which relate to the creation of an entirely new part in the IRDA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This clause mainly updates references in primary legislation for consistency with the provisions and terminology in the new Rules of Court 2021.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For example, references to "plaintiff" in existing legislation are now replaced with "claimant" as per the terminology in the Rules of Court 2021 and so on.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The changes in terminology do not change the meaning of the amended provisions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clause 23 deletes obsolete transitional provisions in four Acts.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These provisions were only intended to operate for a transitional period and are no longer necessary today.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To give an example, section 38 of the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore Act 2001 (IPOS Act) empowers the Minister to repeal or amend any written law that is inconsistent with any provision of the IPOS Act.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The intention of section 38 was to bridge any gap between existing laws and the newly enacted IPOS Act at that point in time.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Hence, section 38 of the IPOS Act is no longer relevant today and can be repealed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For good order, these obsolete provisions will be deleted as they will no longer have to be brought into force.
